issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() should return a double, but the solution implementation declares and returns an int. This mismatch between the specified return type (double) and the implemented return type (int) can confuse students about the expected signature and lead to failing tests or unexpected behavior (loss of fractional students-per-tutor precision).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the implementation match the UML by changing the method signature and return type to double and perform floating-point division. For example: public double getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor() { return (double) getTotalNumberOfStudents() / getNumberOfTutors(); } Alternatively, if an integer result is intended, update the UML/problem text to specify an int return type.
